title: Rice on a chessboard: geometric sequences
examples: How much rice is on the 64th square?

marks.label: Square 64: 9.2×10¹⁸
marks.ask: How much rice is on the 64th square?

explain.say: An old story from India tells of the inventor of chess. The king offered any reward. The inventor asked for rice: 1 grain on the first square, 2 on the next, 4, then 8, doubling every square. The king laughed. Look at the yellow mark: square 10 already has 512 grains.

marks.label: Square 64: 9.2×10¹⁸
marks.ask: How much rice is on the 64th square?

explain.say: Doubling means multiplying by 2 each time. A list made by multiplying by the same number is called a geometric sequence, and that number is the common ratio, here 2. Can you work out square 11?

marks.label: Square 64: 9.2×10¹⁸
marks.ask: How much rice is on the 64th square?

explain.say: 1024! Now look at the cyan mark. By square 20 there are 524288 grains, more than half a million, on one square. The curve is still low, but it is starting to wake up.

marks.label: Square 64: 9.2×10¹⁸
marks.ask: How much rice is on the 64th square?

explain.say: The rule: square n holds 2 to the power n minus 1 grains. So square 64 holds 2 to the power 63, about 9.2 billion billion grains. Look at the purple mark, shooting off the top. The king stopped laughing!

marks.label: Square 64: 9.2×10¹⁸
marks.ask: How much rice is on the 64th square?

explain.say: Well done! Adding all 64 squares gives about 18 billion billion grains, more rice than the whole world grows in hundreds of years. That is the power of multiplying, and why compound interest and viruses can grow so fast.

marks.label: Square 64: 9.2×10¹⁸
marks.ask: How much rice is on the 64th square?

faq.a: A list of numbers where you multiply by the same amount each time, like 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The amount is called the common ratio.

faq.q: How much rice is on the 64th square?
faq.a: 2 to the power 63 grains, which is about 9.2 times 10 to the 18, over nine billion billion grains.
It is the number you multiply by to get the next term. Divide any term by the one before it. For 3, 12, 48 it is 4.
asks: How do I find the common ratio?

faq.q: How do you find the nth term of a geometric sequence?
faq.a: Use first term times ratio to the power n minus 1. For 1, 2, 4, 8, the nth term is 2 to the power n minus 1.
asks: What is the formula for a geometric sequence?

faq.q: How much rice is on the whole chessboard?
faq.a: All 64 squares add up to 2 to the power 64 minus 1, about 1.8 times 10 to the 19 grains: far more than the world could ever store.
asks: What is the total of the chessboard rice?

facts: The nth term of a geometric sequence is arⁿ⁻¹, where a is the first term and r the common ratio.
The total number of grains on all 64 squares is 2⁶⁴ − 1 = 18 446 744 073 709 551 615.

quiz.show: What is the common ratio of 5, 15, 45, 135, …?
quiz.why: 15 ÷ 5 = 3, and each term is 3 times the last.
